Cross-ref (June borrowing, from morning cache): https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cx2vd3qgjy9o
(Approved carriers — Yahoo Finance UK analyst commentary + BBC borrowing data)
UK 10-year gilt yields remain the highest in the G7, pinned near 5% after PM Burnham's remarks about using "any flexibility" within the fiscal rules unsettled bond markets on Monday. June public borrowing was 16bn pounds, some 7.9bn below a year earlier but still above official forecasts.
Arend Kapteyn (UBS): if Burnham's government adheres to the existing fiscal rules, "gilt yields could rally by at least 20bp"; changing the rules could push the risk premium materially higher.
IFS (Helen Miller, from morning cache): the government has "found funding for this year, but only by reallocating savings that haven't yet been made," questioning how the giveaways are paid for "next year and the year after." Chancellor John Healey has committed to the previous fiscal rules. Budget due in the autumn.
